files.about: End-to-end API tests with LiteLLM's completion call stubbed (no network).
Circuit breaker state machine: every transition, driven by a fake clock.
Live-mode console endpoints: simulated providers, request traces, key holds, budget overrides, config
The console's Evals screen reads demo/data/*.json; they must match what the repo's eval code produces now.
The console's demo mode (demo/engine.py request path and api()), run under CPython with the same modules
The browser demo's engine, run under CPython: same router modules Pyodide loads, simulated providers.
Eval harness (simulated providers only: no real model is called here) and shadow mode through the API.
Application keys hashed at rest: storage, lookup, pepper, API surface, and migration of a v0.5 database.
Latency-aware ordering and the provider fallback chain (no HTTP, no LiteLLM).
MCP tool gateway: policy core, and the HTTP proxy against a fake MCP server on a real local port.
Policy-as-code: schema, layer combination, evaluation, OPA (fake server over real HTTP), and the API path.
PII detection, content hooks, the opt-in content log and the hash-chained audit trail. All data is fictional.
Semantic cache: embedder, guards, partitions, TTL/LRU, calibration (bundled fictional pairs), and the API path.
Token estimation, TPM limiter, budget hierarchy, showback aggregation (pure functions).
v0.4: streaming (with real LiteLLM mock chunks), response cache, metrics, schema migration.
v0.5 end to end through the HTTP API, LiteLLM stubbed (no network, no provider keys).
